source.title: Beyond Linear Superposition: Discovering Climate Features in AI Weather Models with KAN-SAE

page_placements.theme: Removing shrinkage or dead latents need not reduce error

record.tranche_reason: Compares a nonlinear SAE architecture with a linear SAE and reports reconstruction fidelity, bearing on whether changing SAE architecture reduces reconstruction error. It does not apply the original dark-matter analyses.
record.gate_note: The study does not analyze SAE error vectors, predictability from input activations, token-level error norms or overlap, model-loss effects of reconstruction replacement, or the function of the error term. The reported explained-variance comparison is the only result directly relevant to the training-artifact version. Feature-utilization, redundancy, steering, and circuit results concern learned SAE features, not the reconstruction error.
record.test_reason: The study builds a new SAE variant (B-spline encoder) for a weather transformer and compares it with a linear SAE on feature metrics and explained variance. It never examines the SAE error term: not its linear predictability, not per-token norms across sizes, not loss effects of splicing, not its function. The one fidelity number (r1) is the study's own method against a baseline, from a single setting. The new architecture is aimed at feature utilisation, not at reducing error, so it cannot show whether dark matter is a training artifact. It does not cite or use the dark-matter finding. It only discusses limits of linear SAE assumptions in general.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that B-spline per-feature activations give far more alive features (95.2% vs 55.5%) and lower redundancy at slightly lower explained variance, which they call comparable or 'high' fidelity. They claim nonlinear activations are essential for interpretability of weather models and recover climate features (EU heatwave, typhoon) that linear SAEs miss, supported by steering and circuit case studies.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a B-spline-activation SAE with a linear ReLU SAE; it does not measure linear predictability or cross-size consistency of SAE errors.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported reconstruction-fidelity comparison is between KAN-SAE and L IN-SAE, with KAN-SAE lower in explained variance.

fits_no_version.finding: On SONNY Layer 5 with M=1024, replacing ReLU with per-feature B-spline activations lowered explained variance from 86.6% to 84.2%. Dead features fell from 44.5% to 4.8% and mean L1 fell 24%. Reducing dead latents through the encoder did not reduce reconstruction error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the SAE encoder nonlinearity to revive dead latents does not by itself reduce reconstruction error (observed in a weather-model SAE).

record.problems: Only one weather model and Layer 5 are studied. The reconstruction comparison is aggregate explained variance; no error-vector analyses or uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors note that generalisation to other layers, models, and phenomena remains to be shown.
record.rows_left_out: Feature utilisation, dead-feature rate, activation norms, redundancy, climate-feature localisation, steering, and circuit analyses were left out because they do not measure the SAE reconstruction error or the effects specified in the claim.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of SAE error from input activations: not examined.
Per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, shared failure contexts, persistence with scale: not examined (only one dictionary size, M=1024).
Loss effect of splicing in reconstructions versus random errors of the same size: not examined.
Split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts, and how each responds to dictionary learning: not examined.
Whether steering and circuit analyses lose behaviour without the error term: not examined; steering adds decoder directions only and never measures error contribution.

Whether the error comes from sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents or objective, and whether better or end-to-end-trained SAEs shrink it: not isolated. One encoder swap gave slightly lower EV, while dead latents fell from 44.5% to 4.8%.

record.verdict_notes: Not an LLM study. The SAE is on a 20.5M-parameter weather transformer (SONNY). The reader's V6 limits_scope label is removed: an EV comparison between the study's own method and its baseline, at one size, gives no measure of how much error comes from training choices. No uncertainty is reported, and only one SAE size, layer and model are used.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, shared failure contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether replacing activations with SAE reconstructions harms model loss more than same-size random errors.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error is qualitatively different or resists dictionary learning.
Whether SAE-feature analyses lose behavior when the error term is omitted.

The study compares SAE architectures and reports aggregate reconstruction fidelity, but does not establish whether dark matter mostly originates in training choices, isolate sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents, or objective effects, or test end-to-end training.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Compared explained variance of Layer-5 activations reconstructed by KAN-SAE and L IN-SAE.
rows.note: KAN-SAE has lower explained variance than the linear baseline, a 2.4-point gap that the authors describe as modest. This compares reconstruction fidelity, not the structure or cause of the error.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (KAN-SAE, EV 84.2%) with its baseline (LIN-SAE, EV 86.6%) at one size, one layer and one model. A single aggregate explained-variance comparison between two encoders cannot show whether SAE error mostly comes from training choices. The architecture was not designed to reduce error. It belongs under fits_no_version, not as evidence on V6. Subject should read 'SONNY' (a weather transformer, not a language model).

source_check.problem: Accurate method-versus-baseline benchmark, but it fits no claim version and should not be retained as a phenomenon result row.

relation.reason: Discusses SAE representation and encoder limitations, without testing error predictability, scaling, functional consequences or the causes of dark matter.

tranche.reason: Feature quality and aggregate reconstruction fidelity comparisons neither test nor use any specified dark-matter claim version.

source_check.notes: The study measures reconstruction MSE and explained variance, but not the error properties specified by V1–V6. Evaluation states 51 held-out days, whereas Figure 2 and its discussion use 53 days.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: KAN-SAE versus L IN-SAE on S ONNY Layer 5
reader_labels.reason: The nonlinear architecture improves other reported feature metrics, but its explained variance is lower than the linear baseline (r1), so this comparison does not show reconstruction error shrinking with that architectural change.
